title: Panel-local deictic forms reset at visual panel boundaries
summary: Test whether deictic-like complete wholes refer to the current visual panel and reset when a new panel begins, rather than carrying one global referent across adjacent panels.

design.mechanism: A panel-local index binds to the active diagram unit and is reintroduced after a panel boundary.
design.unit: admitted panel boundary with adjacent label/prose occurrences of the candidate whole
design.contrast: within-panel continuation versus first occurrence after a panel boundary, matched by register and line position
design.prediction: After a boundary, candidate occurrences show renewed local-owner compatibility and reduced continuation to the prior panel; within-panel occurrences preserve the prior owner.
design.falsifier: Held panels show no boundary interaction, or owner compatibility is unchanged after controlling register/position.
design.scope: admitted visual selectors plus cached labels; feasibility_unknown for enough repeated candidate occurrences
design.related: GDT790/GDT791 panel-owner work supplies boundaries but does not test deictic reset; distinct from line-break/reset and register-handoff proposals
